llm.summary: The package claims to be an SSL/TLS certificate inspector, but the included script implements only a local entry-management tool and does not perform any certificate checks — the behavior and declared capabilities do not match.

dimensions.detail: The skill is described as an SSL/TLS certificate checker (commands: check, expiry, chain, batch) but the shipped script (scripts/script.sh) contains only local data-management commands (init, add, list, show, remove, search, export, stats, config, status, reset). There are no certificate inspections, no network/openssl/python libraries for TLS, and no implementation of the 'check'/'expiry'/'chain' commands described in SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the script disagree about available commands. The runtime script reads/writes only to a per-user data directory ($CERTCHECK_DIR or ~/.local/share/certcheck) and uses python3 for JSON parsing, but the skill metadata declares no required binaries. The instructions promise certificate checks but the script does not perform them; this is scope creep/misdirection.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install specification (instruction-only). A single script file is included; nothing is downloaded from external URLs and no archives are extracted. From an install-surface perspective there is no external code fetch.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No credentials or sensitive environment variables are requested. The script honors CERTCHECK_DIR if set (declared in SKILL.md), which is reasonable. However, the script requires python3 at runtime (used for JSON parsing) but the skill's declared 'required binaries' list is empty — a missing declaration that could cause runtime failures.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request elevated privileges and is not always-enabled. It will create and write to a per-user data directory (default ~/.local/share/certcheck) and can delete its own files via the reset command. That is standard for a local utility but users should be aware it writes to their home directory.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Do not install or run this skill expecting SSL/TLS checks: the included script does not implement any certificate inspection functionality described in the SKILL.md. Before proceeding ask the publisher for the correct implementation or an updated package. If you still want to try it locally, inspect the script yourself and run it in a sandboxed environment (or container) — note it will create ~/.local/share/certcheck with entries.jsonl and config.json and uses python3 (not declared). If you need an SSL certificate checker, prefer a skill or tool whose code actually performs TLS/openssl operations and explicitly declares required binaries and network behavior.
